# Crawldad

> Crawldad runs one JSON "payload" — a small, JSON-Schema'd browser-automation DSL — against a headless
> browser and returns a caller-shaped result. The whole product is unusually machine-describable: a typed
> payload language plus a small HTTP surface, so an LLM can author a payload and drive a run from these
> files alone.

A payload is one JSON document (`crawldad`/`name`/`inputs`/`config`/`vars`/`steps`/`result`). Only leaf
expressions are strings in a small, pure, non-Turing-complete expression language; all structure is JSON.
Every payload is validated against the JSON Schema at save time, so a schema-valid payload has a bounded,
inspectable effect surface. Authenticate every request with `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>` or
`X-Api-Key: <api-key>`.

## Docs

- [API reference](docs/API.md): the single, self-contained consumer reference — auth, the run lifecycle in all three shapes (sync result / async 202 / queued 202 + promotion), `GET /runs/{id}`, SSE, cancel, replay, payload CRUD/revisions/diff, queue stats, and the complete wire-code table with the config knob behind every limit. Read this top-to-bottom to author a payload and drive a run.
- [Payload JSON Schema](schema/crawldad-1.schema.json): the normative DSL reference — every node and field carries a `description`. Served live and anonymously at `GET /schema/crawldad-1.schema.json` (media type `application/schema+json`); usable directly as an editor `$schema` target.
- [OpenAPI description](openapi.json): the generated OpenAPI 3.1 spec for the HTTP envelope — every endpoint, its auth, the request/response contracts, and the status codes (including the `202` queued/running run shapes and `429 queue_depth_exceeded`). Served live and anonymously at `GET /openapi.json`; payload request bodies `$ref` the schema above rather than restating the DSL.

## Examples

Curated, schema-valid payloads (each validated in CI against the schema). Commentary for each is in the API reference's Examples section.

- [first-search.json](docs/examples/first-search.json): the gentle intro — navigate, conditional `fill`, `waitForRequest` postback, `locate` + a `for` loop, extract rows.
- [extract-location.json](docs/examples/extract-location.json): the expression language at work — `guard`, `forEach`, and a `switch` over an address block's `<br>` count.
- [download-attachment.json](docs/examples/download-attachment.json): the `download` node streaming to a `storageTarget`, with content-addressed `stored:true` dedup.
- [login-and-search.json](docs/examples/login-and-search.json): the newer surface — `fill.secret` (a vault-resolved credential), a `screenshot` node, structured role/text/xpath selectors, and a checkpointed `while` loop that resumes after a restart.
- [search-pagination.json](docs/examples/search-pagination.json): a full checkpointed pagination crawl (`while` do-loop, `checkpoint`/`resume`, nested `for` loops, `break`, result shaping).
- [scrape-record.json](docs/examples/scrape-record.json): the comprehensive end-to-end scrape — `guard`, `frame`, `switch`, `download`, and deeply nested loops building one nested result object.

## Optional

- [Engine & runtime spec](docs/SPEC.md): the run engine's behavioral contract — execution model, error taxonomy, timeout hierarchy, resource limits, the trace/event model, checkpoints, and the backend adapter interface.
- [Payload language spec](docs/PAYLOAD_SPEC.md): the DSL semantics behind the schema — action set, selectors, control flow, and the expression language with its enumerated builtins.
- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the system architecture (C4 diagrams + run lifecycle) and the Azure infrastructure reference.
- [Threat model](docs/THREAT_MODEL.md): credential scrubbing, credentials-by-reference (`secretRef`), tenant isolation, and PII handling.
